facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s developed asthenia, anorexia, and cough
Six days later, he was hospitalized with diffuse bilateral pneumonia
Numerous 3- to 6-mm pseudovesicular papules with superficial crusting were noted on the trunk
The papules were asymptomatic
Within 48 hours the papules evolved to an extensive, but not confluent, purpuric rash

Nasopharyngeal swab using real-time reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) - Diagnostic testing on superficial skin sample for herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and SARS-CoV-2 viruses (all negative)
Immunohistochemical testing for herpes simplex and varicella zoster viruses (negative)
RT-PCR testing of fixed skin tissue for SARS-CoV-2 (negative)
Histologic analysis showed: - Extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis
Large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration
Dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes and eosinophils in superficial dermis
Early-stage vasculitic alterations with endothelial swelling of dermal vessels without fibrinoid necrosis or thrombosis

rationales.F05: The presence of a purpuric rash is highly suggestive of vasculitis, particularly cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis.
rationales.F09: Extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis is a characteristic histopathological feature of certain dermatological conditions, including vasculitis.
rationales.F11: The presence of a dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes and eosinophils is indicative of an inflammatory process, such as vasculitis.
rationales.F12: Early-stage vasculitic alterations with endothelial swelling of dermal vessels are consistent with a diagnosis of vasculitis, particularly cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including the evolution of papules to a purpuric rash and histologic findings of extensive epidermal necrosis, acantholysis, and perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, are most consistent with Cutaneous Small-Vessel Vasculitis, which is a subtype of vasculitis that specifically affects the small blood vessels in the skin.
